elements.title: Figure 13.—Value of Old Scrap Domestically Recycled, Imported, and Exported, as a Percentage of Total Old Scrap Value
elements.content:
Chart kind: Stacked bar chart
Y-axis: Percentage of total old scrap value, range from -80 to 100
X-axis: Commodity and total old scrap value, in million dollars
Legend:
- Orange: Old scrap imports
- Blue: Old scrap domestically recycled
- Gray: Old scrap exports (negative values)

Commodities (with total old scrap value in parentheses) and approximate bar values:
- *Antimony (49): 100% recycled, 0% imports, 0% exports
- Lead (2,663): ~97% recycled, ~0% imports, ~-3% exports
- *Zinc (519): ~85% recycled, ~4% imports, ~-9% exports
- *Tin (338): ~83% recycled, ~5% imports, ~-8% exports
- *Nickel (2,353): ~75% recycled, ~20% imports, ~-5% exports
- *Magnesium metal (378): ~75% recycled, ~25% imports, 0% exports
- Iron and steel (34,493): ~70% recycled, ~7% imports, ~-23% exports
- Gold (9,247): ~60% recycled, ~5% imports, ~-35% exports
- *Platinum-group metals (4,963): ~60% recycled, ~20% imports, ~-20% exports
- *Aluminum (9,500): ~45% recycled, ~15% imports, ~-40% exports
- *Cobalt (69): ~45% recycled, ~30% imports, ~-25% exports
- *Chromium (1,068): ~35% recycled, ~25% imports, ~-40% exports
- Copper (6,480): ~20% recycled, ~10% imports, ~-70% exports
- Silver (4,694): ~18% recycled, ~15% imports, ~-70% exports
- *Titanium (306): ~3% recycled, ~80% imports, ~-17% exports
elements.notes:
* Indicates commodity is included in the final 2022 U.S. Critical Minerals List.
Percentages for exports, imports, and domestically recycled old scrap add to 100 percent of the total old scrap value for each commodity. Exports are shown as negative percentages to indicate value of supply lost.
